newsitem.title: USA: Teledesic weighs scaled back design - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Teledesic weighs scaled back design - WSJ.

text.p: Teledesic Corp is exploring a reduced design that would allow its communications system to begin operating with only a third of its planned satellites, the Wall Street Journal said Wednesday.
The $9 billion joint venture, backed by cellular phone mogul Craig McCaw and Microsoft's Bill Gates, would transmit voice, video and computer communications across the globe.

Teledesic hopes it will begin operating in about 2002, but it has met with scepticism because the plan calls for operating 840 satellites in low-earth orbit - a figure about 12 times greater than any other proposed satellite system, the paper said.
Wednesday's report, citing people familiar with the research, said the company is looking at the possibility of starting operations with only 288 satellites in 12 orbital rings around the Earth.

A Teledesic spokesman told the paper the company has not changed its plan to build an 840-satellite system. Others told the paper Teledesic still hopes to build a system that would include many more satellites.
